description: The CIWW research team at Beijing Normal University publishes Python routines for estimating and mapping industrial water withdrawal in China. The Zenodo archive accompanies a GitHub repository with enterprise-level estimation, seasonal allocation, spatial mapping and plotting scripts. The inspected mapping function combines province identifiers, spatial allocation rates and monthly withdrawal tables to produce 672 monthly NetCDF layers for 1965–2020 at 0.1 or 0.25 degree resolution. It also converts volumetric withdrawal to water depth using grid-cell areas. The archived release is free under CC-BY-4.0. These routines can prepare industrial-demand inputs for hydrological and water-supply simulations and explain the companion CIWW dataset. The main limitations require substantial adaptation: the repository has no README, input paths are fixed, and source tables are external. The inspected enterprise script references an undefined f_ind variable, and the two inspected files have empty main blocks. They were read as methodological source code, not executed or verified as ready-to-run software.
